title: Complete Erdős Problem #101: Four-Point Lines from Planar Point Sets (Work in Progress)

problemStatement.formal: n \text{ points in } \mathbb{R}^2,\ \text{no 5 collinear} \implies \#\{\text{lines with exactly 4 points}\} = o(n^2)
problemStatement.plain: Given n points in ℝ² with no five collinear, is the number of lines containing exactly four points o(n²)? Grünbaum: ≫ n^{3/2}. Solymosi–Stojaković: n^{2−O(1/√log n)}. Open.
whyMatters: A central incidence-geometry question; bounds on $k$-rich lines drive extremal combinatorics.
